title: Impact of Grade Retention on Future Academic Performance

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

The most appropriate causal method for this research question is **Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**.

**Reasoning:**
The research scenario describes a situation where grade retention (the treatment) is assigned based on whether a student's end-of-year test score (`running_var`) falls just below a specific cutoff. This creates a sharp, non-random assignment mechanism at the cutoff point. Students scoring just below the cutoff are retained, while students scoring just above are not. RDD exploits this discontinuity in treatment assignment to estimate the causal effect. By comparing the future academic performance (`y`) of students immediately above and below the cutoff, we can isolate the effect of grade retention, assuming other factors vary smoothly around the cutoff.

**Key Assumption:**
The primary assumption for a valid RDD is the **continuity of potential outcomes** at the cutoff. This means that, in the absence of the treatment (grade retention), the average future academic performance of students would evolve smoothly across the cutoff. Any observed jump or discontinuity in average future performance at the cutoff can then be causally attributed to the grade retention policy. This assumption implicitly requires that students cannot precisely manipulate their scores to fall on one side of the cutoff, which can be checked using a density test of the running variable.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Install and load necessary packages
if (!requireNamespace("rdrobust", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("rdrobust")
}
if (!requireNamespace("rddensity", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("rddensity")
}
if (!requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("dplyr")
}

library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(dplyr)

# Data file path
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s97_data.csv"

# Read the data
df <- read.csv(data_path)

# Verify cutoff logic:
# The problem states "retaining students who score just below a cutoff".
# The preview shows:
#   - running_var -0.0204, treated 1 (implies retained, score below cutoff)
#   - running_var 0.0721, treated 0 (implies not retained, score above cutoff)
# This indicates the running_var is already centered around the cutoff of 0.
# So, treated = 1 if running_var < 0, and treated = 0 if running_var >= 0.

cat("--- RDD Main Analysis: Impact of Grade Retention on Future Academic Performance ---\n")
# RDD estimation using rdrobust package
# y: outcome variable (future test scores)
# x: running variable (end-of-year test scores, centered)
# c: cutoff point (0 in this case)
rdd_result <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0)

# Print the full summary of the RDD results
print(rdd_result)

cat("\n--- Basic Robustness Checks ---\n")

# Robustness Check 1: McCrary Density Test for Manipulation of Running Variable
# Checks for any significant discontinuity in the density of the running variable at the cutoff.
# A jump would suggest agents can precisely sort themselves, invalidating RDD.
cat("\n1. McCrary Density Test (Manipulation Check):\n")
mccrary_result <- rddensity(x = df$running_var, c = 0)
print(mccrary_result)
cat("Interpretation: A large p-value (e.g., > 0.05) suggests no significant manipulation of the running variable around the cutoff.\n")

# Robustness Check 2: Varying Bandwidth
# The rdrobust package automatically selects an optimal bandwidth.
# Running the analysis with smaller and larger bandwidths checks the sensitivity of the results.
optimal_h_left <- rdd_result$h[1, 1] # Optimal bandwidth for the left side
optimal_h_right <- rdd_result$h[1, 2] # Optimal bandwidth for the right side

cat(paste0("\n2. Sensitivity to Bandwidth:\n"))
cat(paste0("   Optimal bandwidths (left, right): (", round(optimal_h_left, 4), ", ", round(optimal_h_right, 4), ")\n"))

# Half the optimal bandwidth
h_half_left <- optimal_h_left / 2
h_half_right <- optimal_h_right / 2
cat(paste0("   Running RDD with half optimal bandwidth (h_l = ", round(h_half_left, 4), ", h_r = ", round(h_half_right, 4), ")\n"))
rdd_half_h <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0, h = c(h_half_left, h_half_right))
cat(paste0("   Coefficient with half bandwidth: ", round(rdd_half_h$coef[1], 4), "\n"))

# Double the optimal bandwidth
h_double_left <- optimal_h_left * 2
h_double_right <- optimal_h_right * 2
cat(paste0("   Running RDD with double optimal bandwidth (h_l = ", round(h_double_left, 4), ", h_r = ", round(h_double_right, 4), ")\n"))
rdd_double_h <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = 0, h = c(h_double_left, h_double_right))
cat(paste0("   Coefficient with double bandwidth: ", round(rdd_double_h$coef[1], 4), "\n"))
